prelimsCapsule.coreConceptSummary: The SPSC acts as the watchdog of the merit system in the state. Established under Articles 315-323, it is a constitutional body responsible for conducting examinations for appointments to state services and advising the Governor on disciplinary/service matters.
highYieldFacts: Fact 1: The Chairman and members are appointed by the Governor but can only be removed by the President of India.
Fact 2: Tenure is 6 years or until the age of 62, whichever is earlier.
Fact 3: The SPSC presents an annual report of its work to the Governor, who places it before the State Legislature.
Fact 4: The expenses, including salaries and pensions, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Fact 5: The President can extend the functions of an SPSC if requested by two or more states.
trapsAndElimination: Trap 1: Confusion in removal power; the Governor appoints them, but only the President has the authority to remove them based on SC inquiry (Art 317).
Trap 2: Eligibility for further employment; on ceasing to hold office, the SPSC Chairman is eligible for appointment as Chairman of UPSC or other SPSC, but not for any other employment under Govt.
keyArticlesOrStatutes: Articles 315 to 323 of the Indian Constitution

mainsFramework.inDepthTheoryHtml:
Institutional Architecture and Governance Role

The State Public Service Commission (SPSC) is a critical constitutional pillar designed to uphold the meritocratic recruitment process within state administrative structures. Its independence is ensured through constitutional safeguards similar to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC).

  • Functional Autonomy: The SPSC acts as an advisory body. While its advice on disciplinary matters is not binding, the Supreme Court has emphasized that the government should have strong reasons to deviate from it.
  • Recruitment Integrity: The core mandate is to conduct competitive examinations, ensuring transparency and impartiality in the selection of Class I and II state officers.
  • Contemporary Challenges:
    • Political Patronage: Allegations of political influence in the appointment of chairpersons and members often undermine the institutional image.
    • Procedural Delays: Frequent paper leaks and litigation-led delays in result declarations have eroded public trust.
    • Lack of Autonomy in Budgeting: While salaries are charged to the Consolidated Fund, operational budgets are often subject to state executive discretion.

The Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2nd ARC) has consistently recommended that SPSC members must have a track record of impeccable integrity and domain expertise to effectively oversee the recruitment apparatus of the state.

prelims.question: Which of the following are the functions of the State Public Service Commission?
options: Advising the Governor on disciplinary matters
prelims.explanation: SPSCs advise on recruitment and discipline but policy-making regarding reservation is a prerogative of the State Legislature/Executive.

mains.question: The institutional independence of State Public Service Commissions is vital for the health of Indian democracy. Analyze the challenges faced by these commissions in current administrative setups.

modelMainsQA.question: Discuss the constitutional provisions governing State Public Service Commissions and analyze the reasons for the recent erosion of their credibility in the eyes of the public. (250 Words, 15 Marks)

approach.intro: Define SPSC as a watchdog of meritocracy under Article 315-323.
approach.body: Detail constitutional safeguards (Appointment, Tenure, Expenses). Contrast with current challenges (nepotism, corruption, leaks).
approach.conclusion: Suggest reform-oriented measures like professionalization of selection and 2nd ARC recommendations.

modelMainsQA.modelAnswerHtml:
Model Answer

Introduction: The State Public Service Commission (SPSC) is a constitutional body (Articles 315-323) serving as the guarantor of the merit-based system in state governance, analogous to the UPSC at the Union level.

Constitutional Safeguards

  • Security of Tenure: Though appointed by the Governor, members can only be removed by the President for 'misbehavior' following a Supreme Court inquiry.
  • Financial Independence: Expenses are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State.
  • Prohibition on Post-retirement Employment: Prevents 'quid-pro-quo' arrangements with the state government.

Reasons for Credibility Erosion

  • Political Patronage: Appointments are often perceived as rewards for loyalists rather than for domain experts (highlighted in Salil Sabhlok Case).
  • Operational Inefficiency: Repeated cases of question paper leaks and litigation-marred recruitment cycles.
  • Lack of Transparency: Opaque selection criteria and delays in the annual report submission to the legislature.

Way Forward

The 2nd ARC recommended adopting a transparent search committee model for appointing members. Digitization of recruitment processes and adhering to a fixed 'recruitment calendar' are essential to restore public trust and constitutional morality.

practiceMCQs.question: Regarding the removal of a member of SPSC, which of the following is correct?
options: The Governor can remove them for misconduct
The President can remove them only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court
The State Legislature can remove them by a two-thirds majority
The Chairman of UPSC can remove them
practiceMCQs.answer: The President can remove them only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court
practiceMCQs.explanation: Article 317 specifies the removal process for SPSC members to ensure insulation from local political pressure.

practiceMCQs.question: Can the SPSC be abolished by the State Legislature?
options: No, it is a constitutional body
Only with the consent of the President
Only if the Supreme Court permits
practiceMCQs.answer: No, it is a constitutional body
practiceMCQs.explanation: As a Constitutional body, it cannot be abolished by a simple state law; any change in its structure would require a Constitutional Amendment.
